title: Renal Disorders, Part 3: Tubular disease, cysts, AKI, enuresis, hypertension

sections.title: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
notes: Distal nephron **ignores ADH**: dilute urine, **hypernatremia**, high serum osmolality. 90% **X-linked recessive**. Secondary: drugs, pyelonephritis, obstruction, **sickle cell trait**.
Vague in infants: poor feeding, failure to thrive, irritability, constipation. Breastfed babies are diagnosed later (lower solute load).
Red flags: can't toilet train, daytime accidents, **constant thirst**, dilated bladder on ultrasound.

sections.title: DI diagnosis and treatment
notes: **Vasopressin test**: urine concentrates in central DI, **no change in nephrogenic**. ADH normal or high in nephrogenic, low in central.
Sodium up to 170, serum osmolality over 300.
**Never restrict water**. Low sodium and protein diet, **thiazide** and **indomethacin** reduce water loss.

sections.title: Bartter syndrome
notes: **Loop of Henle** defect (like a loop diuretic). Can start **in utero with polyhydramnios**, triangular face, polyuria, failure to thrive.
**High renin and aldosterone with normal or low BP**. **Hypokalemic hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis**, **hypercalciuria** (stones), low magnesium in 30%, high urine chloride and prostaglandins.
Treat: fluids, potassium, spironolactone, ACE inhibitor, **indomethacin**, growth hormone.

sections.title: Bartter vs Gitelman
notes: Gitelman: **distal tubule** (like a thiazide), presents in late childhood to adulthood with cramps, numbness, fatigue. Growth delay is a Bartter feature.
Both: hypokalemic hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis. **Urine calcium high in Bartter, low in Gitelman**. Magnesium **always low in Gitelman**.

sections.title: Polycystic kidney disease
notes: **Autosomal recessive**: oligohydramnios, **pulmonary hypoplasia, Potter facies**, bilateral flank masses in newborns, **hepatic fibrosis with portal hypertension**, cholangitis.
**Autosomal dominant**: adults, hematuria, flank masses, hypertension, cysts in liver, pancreas, spleen, **intracranial aneurysms**. No family history doesn't rule it out (new mutations).

sections.title: Nephronophthisis and Bardet-Biedl
notes: Nephronophthisis: medullary cysts, early **polyuria, thirst, fatigue**, anemia (low EPO). **End-stage kidney disease around age 13**. Joubert (oculomotor apraxia, retinitis pigmentosa, ataxia). Ultrasound: lost corticomedullary differentiation.
**Bardet-Biedl** (Laurence-Moon-Bardet-Biedl): obesity, **retinitis pigmentosa**, hypogonadism, **polydactyly**, intellectual disability, cystic dysplastic kidneys.

sections.title: Multicystic dysplastic kidney
notes: Renal mass is the most common newborn abdominal mass: **hydronephrosis first, MCDK second**. Bilateral is fatal.
Confirm with ultrasound, then **VCUG** (30 to 50% have reflux in the other kidney).
**Serial ultrasounds**: the kidney should shrink. If it grows, refer for nephrectomy. Normal life expectancy, **avoid contact sports**.

sections.title: Acute kidney injury: types
notes: Rapid fall in filtration: rising creatinine and BUN, oliguria.
**Prerenal**: low perfusion (**gastroenteritis and dehydration most common**, heart failure, sepsis). **Postrenal**: obstruction. **Intrinsic**: HUS, rhabdomyolysis, aminoglycosides.

sections.title: Prerenal and postrenal indices
notes: Healthy tubules hold on to sodium and water: **urine sodium under 10 to 20, FENa under 1%** (under 2% in newborns), **urine osmolality over 400** (over 350 in newborns), **BUN to creatinine over 20**.
Untreated prerenal or long obstruction turns into intrinsic injury.

sections.title: Intrinsic AKI indices
notes: Damaged tubules: **FENa over 2%** (over 2.5% in newborns), high urine sodium, **dilute urine**, **BUN to creatinine under 15**.
Sloughed tubule cells: **muddy brown granular casts**.

sections.title: AKI staging, workup and management
notes: Failure: creatinine 3 times baseline or urine under 0.5 mL/kg/h. Over 4 weeks: loss of function. Over 3 months: end-stage disease.
Labs: BMP, urinalysis, **urine sodium**. Renal ultrasound for anatomy.
Prevent: hydration with NSAIDs, monitor **gentamicin and vancomycin levels**. Bolus **20 mL/kg** (10 mL/kg if cardiac). Treat acidosis and hyperkalemia (watch T waves and QRS, insulin and glucose).
**Dialysis**: fluid overload over 10 to 20%, severe acidosis, hyperkalemia, **BUN over 100** or symptomatic uremia.

sections.title: Intrinsic AKI keywords
notes: Muddy brown casts: **acute tubular necrosis** (aminoglycosides, methotrexate, contrast, myoglobin).
Hematuria **2 to 3 weeks after strep**, hypertension, **low C3, normal C4**: post-infectious GN.
Gross hematuria **during a URI (1 to 3 days)**, **normal C3 and C4**: IgA nephropathy.
Rash, arthritis, serositis, **low C3 and C4**, ANA and anti-dsDNA: lupus nephritis.

sections.title: Vasculitis and other intrinsic causes
notes: Hemoptysis plus **anti-GBM**: Goodpasture. Sinusitis, epistaxis, **c-ANCA**: granulomatosis with polyangiitis. Lungs plus **p-ANCA**: microscopic polyangiitis. Asthma, eosinophilia, p-ANCA: eosinophilic granulomatosis (Churg-Strauss).
Fast loss of function with **crescents** on biopsy: rapidly progressive GN, emergency biopsy.
**Fever, rash, eosinophilia** with urine eosinophils and WBC casts: **allergic interstitial nephritis**.
Bloody diarrhea, anemia, low platelets, schistocytes, high LDH: **diarrhea-positive HUS** (Shiga toxin E coli).

sections.title: Nocturnal enuresis: definition and workup
notes: Strong family history. More common in boys. Usually dry by about 6 in girls, 8 in boys.
Diagnosis of exclusion. History of evening fluids, daytime voiding, number of wet nights.
**Urinalysis first**: glucose (diabetes), **low specific gravity (DI)**, WBC or positive culture (UTI).

sections.title: Enuresis differential
notes: Overactive bladder: urgency, crossing legs, **squatting with heel in the perineum**. Neurogenic bladder, small bladder capacity, nocturnal polyuria, cystitis.
**Obstructive sleep apnea**: removing tonsils and adenoids can cure it. Seizures. **Ectopic ureter: never dry**. Constipation, diabetes mellitus or insipidus.
Expected bladder capacity = **30 mL + (age x 30 mL)**. Nocturnal polyuria if night urine over 130% of that.

sections.title: Enuresis treatment
notes: Reassure, self-limited. Restrict **evening** fluids but hydrate in the day. No treatment before age 6. Reward dry nights, never punish.
**First line: bed-wetting alarm**, 8 to 12 weeks. Then **desmopressin** at bedtime: **no drinking after the dose** (hyponatremia, seizures).
Overactive bladder: **oxybutynin** (anticholinergic). Sleep apnea: lateral neck x-ray, ENT.

sections.title: Hypertension: measuring
notes: Case: 12-year-old with repeat BP 128/77, **over the 95th percentile**: hypertension.
Rest 5 minutes, bare arm at heart level, child calm. **Bladder length 80 to 100% and width 40% of mid-arm circumference**. Too small a cuff reads falsely high.
Confirm with a **manual reading on 3 occasions**. Not in hospitalized children.

sections.title: Hypertension: causes
notes: **Before puberty: mostly secondary**. After puberty: mostly essential, but look for a cause at any age.
Chest pain or murmur: coarctation. Weight loss, sweating, flushing: hyperthyroidism, **pheochromocytoma**, CAH. Headache, papilledema: brain tumour. Rash, joints: lupus.
Echo for coarctation. Renal ultrasound: masses (Wilms, neuroblastoma), polycystic or small kidneys.
Drugs: steroids, **decongestants and cold medicines**, NSAIDs, OCPs, stimulants, isotretinoin.

sections.title: Syndromes and treatment of hypertension
notes: Williams: supravalvar aortic stenosis, renal artery stenosis. Turner: coarctation. Tuberous sclerosis, **neurofibromatosis (renal artery stenosis)**, polycystic kidneys.
Lifestyle: weight loss, **1 hour of exercise daily**, screen time under 2 hours, less salt and sugary drinks.
First line drugs: **ACE inhibitors or calcium channel blockers** (also ARBs, beta blockers, diuretics). Start low, add a second agent if needed.
